title: Khmer Rouge

endonym.native: ខ្មែរក្រហម

capsule: Democratic Kampuchea was the state established by the Khmer Rouge after their capture of Phnom Penh on 17 April 1975, led by Pol Pot, Nuon Chea, Ieng Sary, and Khieu Samphan. The regime immediately evacuated cities, abolished money and private property, imposed forced agricultural collectivization, and targeted Buddhist monks, ethnic minorities, and the educated; the resulting death toll is estimated at 1.5–2 million people, roughly 25 percent of Cambodia's population. Vietnam invaded in December 1978 and captured Phnom Penh on 7 January 1979, dismantling the regime, though Khmer Rouge forces continued guerrilla resistance along the Thai border for nearly two more decades.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The territorial extent of Democratic Kampuchea is the internationally recognized borders of Cambodia for the period 1975–1979 and is precisely attested.
